claims.statement: TVI-CAMS is an internal multi-tenant working layer for TVI schools running TESDA TWSP/CFSP scholarship batches; the tool never holds official standing (TESDA SIS/T2MIS/BSRS remain authoritative) and UI copy must never imply official approval or submission (RULES rule 27).

RLS is the security boundary and UI hiding is usability only — every authorization decision is made by Postgres RLS via app_private.* helper functions (RULES §1.1), and a JS-side tenant filter is a bug even when it returns the right answer because it signals the query was written assuming no RLS (RULES §1.2).

No statement may be executed against the live Supabase project without explicit user permission (RULES §10, [deny] via .claude/settings.json permissions.deny): the rule covers execute_sql including read-only selects, apply_migration, branch create/merge/reset, and edge-function deploys by any route (MCP, CLI, psql), because there is one hosted project and no staging, so an unreviewed statement lands on real tenant data; schema questions are answered from the checked-in migrations and database.types.ts first.

supabase/migrations/README.md records every migration in its first state table as both recorded and present (20260904120000 and 20260910120000 repair-recorded, 20260906120000 applied transactionally) and its 2026-10-24 block records 20261024071359 (ADR-007) as applied with four column assertions verified, but that ledger stops there: both later checked-in migrations, 20261024110000 (ADR-008 billing_deadline) and 20261111120000 (T2MIS terminal-report fields), carry their own `NOT APPLIED — RULES.md rule 36` header and appear in no state table, so both are checked in and unapplied until someone verifies otherwise.

The evidence upload I/O in modules/documents/data/evidence.ts (the private compliance-evidence bucket, signed-URL reads) is written but not exercised: two dashboard toggles (Clerk's Supabase integration and Supabase Third-Party Auth) are still unset under issue #122, so every call fails with an RLS denial indistinguishable from a code defect, and the file must not be debugged against a live project until #122 is closed.

The blocker-gate family (blockingDocuments, blockerCount, blockingDocumentNames) in modules/documents/domain/compliance.ts implements ADR-004 D4 and is unit-tested in tests/unit/doc-blockers.test.ts, but no screen or other code consumes it — it is a ready public domain surface, not live screen behavior.

After any migration (RULES §3 rule 20) the agent must regenerate lib/supabase/database.types.ts and then update the affected mappers and domain types; new migrations are additive with 20260528160300 canonical. supabase/migrations/README.md is what gets updated in the same PR, and a row moves to applied only once a migration has actually run — docs/DATA_MODEL.md stops at seven versions and is history.

Neither the supabase/migrations/ directory listing nor list_migrations alone is authoritative: Supabase keys applied migrations on the version string, so renaming a file makes it look unapplied and hand-run SQL records nothing, and that drift has already happened twice (20260906114735 and 20261024071359 were both renamed to the version Supabase recorded). Objects must be confirmed by name (pg_proc, pg_policies); a policy-set comparison reads as a match no matter what is missing. One policy, public.tenants' "Tenants selectable by Clerk user", is defined by no checked-in migration and omits the is_active check its reviewed counterpart enforces.

The checked schema now extends past the 2026-09-10 record of 18 tables, 36 foreign keys and seven enums: 20260910120000 adds a seven-table billing domain with 16 foreign keys and the billing_type enum, and the newer 20261024071359 (ADR-007) replaces the fixed max_absences count with max_absence_percent on program_billing_rules and tenant_settings and adds attendance_records.excused, so both the dated recorded shape and the checked-in target belong to a record rather than to a fresh read.

The ADR-006 /schools/new write path creates a tenant plus its registered programs atomically: the Server Action composes the validated SchoolCommand (pure rules in modules/tenancy/domain/schoolDraft.ts) and the write goes through modules/tenancy/data/schools.ts's createSchool, which calls the security invoker public.create_school RPC on the Clerk-scoped anon client (never the service-role client), so RLS still evaluates every statement inside the transaction; the screen is gated on the platform-admin axis via the current_user_is_platform_admin() RPC snapshot (getPlatformAdminSnapshot), deliberately not on resolveRouteRole or tenant role, and results distinguish created / duplicate-code / denied (RLS 42501) / sync-failed / unconfigured.

Platform admin is a separate axis from profile_role, not a fifth role value: it is its own public.platform_admins table (RLS enabled with no policies, so it is unreadable and unwritable through the Clerk-scoped anon client and the role cannot be self-granted), resolved in-app only through the security definer public.current_user_is_platform_admin() boolean. Its reach is the school registry only — tenants, qualifications, tenant_qualifications, unassigned profiles, and seating a tenant's first member (whose INSERT policy carries two load-bearing guards: it cannot seat itself, and only into a memberless tenant) — with no policy granting any compliance table (batches, learners, documents, lamr_*, activity_log); granting one is a boundary change that needs its own ADR (RULES §7, ADR-006 P3).

`pnpm test` is `vitest run` (include `tests/unit/**/*.test.ts` in vitest.config.mts) and `tests/unit/` holds 26 spec files at this head, so rule 34's "no test runner yet / placeholder" prose no longer describes the repo. Time-dependent behavior is pinned with vi.setSystemTime rather than the runner clock (batches.test.ts fixes 2026-06-01 for its daysToBilling block); dashboard-domain.test.ts needs no clock because daysToBilling is precomputed on its fixtures.

The post-sign-in open-redirect defense lives in the pure domain function `sanitizeRedirectUrl` (`modules/auth/domain/redirectUrl.ts`), which `app/sign-in/[[...sign-in]]/sign-in-page.tsx` invokes on the attacker-controlled `redirect_url` query param: a trimmed value passes through only if it is a same-origin relative path (single leading slash, no URL scheme, no protocol-relative `//host` form, no backslash tricks); anything else falls back to "/". All post-verification navigations — the `finalize` callbacks and the `startGoogleSignIn` OAuth attempt — target that sanitized value through Clerk's `decorateUrl` rather than a bare URL.

docs/DATA_MODEL.md stops at seven versions and its prose is history rather than current: it still marks 20260906120000 "genuinely missing" (now applied), says /users/new cannot assign anyone until 20260904120000 runs (now applied and recorded), and frames the pending set as behaviour-only — which no longer holds, since ADR-007 and ADR-008 are checked in and unlisted. supabase/migrations/README.md is the ledger that is current, and it dates its own state blocks (2026-10-04, 2026-10-24) rather than standing as a timeless catalog.

Local development is `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev`; `.env.example` documents the Clerk test keys (`pk_test_*`/`sk_test_*`) used by the e2e suite, the Supabase pair is read as `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` + `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` by `lib/supabase/server.ts`, and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is read only by `lib/supabase/service.ts` for the Clerk webhook; when the Supabase pair is unset, `isSupabaseConfigured()` is false and data functions return `unconfigured` snapshots — the honest empty state, not a bug to paper over.

RULES.md rule 30 fixes the ADR precedence chain one way: ADR-001 supersedes conflicting billing-is-preparation-only PRD/TRD wording, ADR-003 amends ADR-001 §4 (derived packet due_date, P5), ADR-007 supersedes ADR-001's Elig row (20% of total_sessions or 3 consecutive unexcused absences replaces the retired ≥5-absence count), ADR-008 amends ADR-003<|place_holder_mm_span_0442|>P5 for the batch-level deadline only, and ADR-006 supersedes FR-02's "Super Admin is not implemented" while closing platform-admin reach to the school registry — extending it to any compliance table, or letting the operator seat itself into a tenant, needs its own ADR. ADR-002 and ADR-005 stay accepted and load-bearing for scope.

Two schema facts are not wired into any caller: max_absence_percent and attendance_records.excused have no code reference (modules/attendance/domain/eligibility.ts is unbuilt), and modules/batches/data/batches.ts reads `row.billing_deadline ?? null`, so until 20261024110000 is applied every batch reports "not recorded" and no path exists to enter a deadline. Separately, lib/supabase/database.types.ts is out of step in both directions — it lacks the billing tables, `excused` and `max_absence_percent` and still describes `max_absences`, while carrying `billing_deadline` by hand ahead of its migration.

Contrary to any 'green CI is only local' assumption, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `pnpm lint`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm test` on every pull request and every push to `main`, on Node 22 (required, because Vitest 4's rolldown throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` on Node 21 or older before any test loads), needs no secrets, installs with `--frozen-lockfile`, and cancels superseded runs. What it does not run is `pnpm build` and Playwright.

The checks that actually bite inside the shared server client are governed by RULES rule 3: lib/supabase/server.ts builds the anon-key client with Clerk's `accessToken` callback (no template, no hand-set Authorization header), and the callback throws the exported NO_CLERK_TOKEN_MESSAGE when Clerk issues no token so the failure surfaces as `sync-failed` instead of an indistinguishable empty `anon` read. tests/unit/supabase-server.test.ts pins both the callback shape and the throw, and is the pattern to copy for other server-boundary code.

Which checked-in migrations are applied has no trustworthy checked-in answer: neither a `NOT APPLIED` header line nor any wiki sentence is evidence, because checked-in text never runs. The only authority is `list_migrations` plus confirming the named objects, and reaching either is gated by rule 36.

The T2MIS import half of FR-10 is built but has no screen: importLearnersCsv in modules/import-export/data/learnerImport.ts has no caller anywhere in app/, so the report path is the only intended surface. The pipeline is ULI-keyed — a row without a well-formed ULI is rejected because ULI is the permanent learner key, and a duplicate ULI inside one file rejects the later row. The 48 verbatim T2MIS headers live in modules/import-export/domain/t2mis.ts and are pinned by tests/unit/t2mis.test.ts.

modules/batches/data/learners.ts reads the T2MIS roster fields from the one-to-one learner_details table added by migration 20261111120000, embedding it only on the tenant roster fetch (trainers get no learner_details through RLS, which is why the report route redirects them first). The unmigrated schema degrades instead of failing: a row or embed without it maps every cell to '' via `orEmpty`, so null and undefined both read as not-recorded, and the roster query is paged at 1000 rows because the API would otherwise drop the rest of a large school's export silently. The separate qualification-facts query is the strict one — any error, including one caused by the unapplied migration, fails the whole snapshot, because blank qualification cells would be indistinguishable from not-recorded.

Export and import split across two modules rather than one: the 48-column T2MIS layout belongs to modules/import-export/domain/t2mis.ts, while the workbook writer lives in modules/reports/domain/xlsx.ts and the DOM/Blob download in modules/reports/ui/exportXlsx.ts, which also separates an empty result from a failed roster fetch in its toast copy. The report surface is /t/<tenantCode>/(sections)/report and it server-redirects trainers to /trainer, gated on resolveTrustedRole rather than resolveRouteRole so the ?role= preview override cannot bypass the omission boundary.

Tenant context resolves through the URL path segment /t/<tenantCode>, validated against the caller's own memberships before any page under it renders by app/(dashboard)/t/[tenantCode]/layout.tsx — a code that is not one of the caller's schools never falls back to all schools. /schools/new sits outside that segment because school creation needs an actor outside the tenant boundary, and the older unsegmented routes survive only as forwarders through app/(dashboard)/legacy-redirect.tsx.

The report client surfaces live under `app/(dashboard)/t/[tenantCode]/(sections)/` (activity-log, analytics, batch-cards, billing, documents, report, table-view); that directory holds no `layout.tsx`, and the KPI row is not rendered by a section layout. `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` states the KPI row is rendered only by the two dashboard pages.

Auditing which checked-in migrations are applied is not done by reading the files: the only authority is `list_migrations` plus the named objects present, because a migration filename's numeric prefix is the recorded version and a README table is a dated snapshot. `supabase/migrations/README.md` latest block is dated 2026-10-24 and lists only eight files, so it is silent on `20261024110000` and `20261111120000` — both still declared NOT APPLIED by their own headers.

Green CI still proves nothing about authorization: there is no `tests/integration/` or `tests/security/` directory, so every RLS and tenant-isolation claim rests on reading the migration (RULES rule 35). The loop also proves little about authentication — the Supabase client test mocks `createClient` and Clerk's `auth`, pinning how the client is called rather than that Supabase accepts the call — and about the real schema, because unit tests run against the generated `database.types.ts`, which can disagree with the live database.

`pnpm test:e2e` is a separate Playwright run gated on Clerk test credentials: `e2e/auth.spec.ts` obtains a Clerk testing token, visits `/dashboard` and expects a redirect to `/sign-in`, deliberately exercising the `requireAuthenticatedUser()` gate in `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` rather than `proxy.ts`, while `playwright.config.ts` boots the app through `pnpm dev` on `PORT` or `:3000` with `global.setup.ts` as a dependency.

The full verification loop is `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` → `pnpm lint` → `pnpm test` → `pnpm build`, and each step defends a different invariant: tsc alone catches a `DB_TO_UI_STAGE` map missing a variant because the union lives in generated types rather than in a lint rule (rule 18, [types]); lint alone catches an import-direction breach through `import/no-restricted-paths`' four zones — `app → modules → shared → lib/supabase`, `data/` private per module, `shared/` leaf-only, `database.types.ts` for data layers only (rules 7–10, [lint]) — plus a warn-only cyclomatic-complexity 15 signal; test pins behavioral rules including the rule-19 catch-swallowed banner ordering; and `pnpm build` is the only step that compiles Server Components, so a page that typechecks can still fail the RSC boundary.

Checked-in docs drift from the tree in ways that mislead a change: RULES rule 34 says there is no test runner while `tests/unit/` holds 32 specs, and README's Status table still lists CSV import as Planned while `modules/import-export/` is built with no screen, so the ADR chain and application source outrank both (rules 30–31).
